title: I'm building Tiny Prospector with AI help — keeping it playful has taken a lot of iteration
author: Devahard
selftext:
Hey everyone! I've been building Tiny Prospector, a little mining puzzle where you read row and column clues, dig for gold, and decide whether to head back to camp or risk going deeper. The video is a short run from the current alpha.

I've used AI to help with both the code and graphics. My process has been small passes: describe the change I want, work through the implementation or art, try it in the game, then go back over what feels off. I've been checking the desktop and phone layouts along the way too.

One thing that's taken more iteration than I expected is keeping the game playful while making it easy to understand. An earlier Claim selector turned into a wall of text. It worked, but it lost the feeling of choosing a slightly ridiculous place to go mining. I've been moving the choices back into illustrated places around camp and making the mine entrance more obvious. Getting the feature working was only part of it; I still had to judge whether it felt like the game I wanted to make.

I'd love feedback on that balance. Is it clear where to start, and do the clues make sense once you're digging? If you've built something with AI, how do you keep the UI from drifting into generic menus as you add features?

You can try the free browser alpha here: [Tiny Prospector on itch.io](https://devharding-star.itch.io/tiny-prospector)

There are phone betas too:

**Android:** [Join the tester Google Group](https://groups.google.com/g/tiny-prospector-android-beta), then [opt in on Google Play](https://play.google.com/apps/testing/com.devonharding.tinyprospector) and install. Please use the same Google account for both. You don't need to send me your email directly. If you're able to stay opted in and play during the 14-day closed test, that would really help.

**iPhone / iPad:** [Join on TestFlight](https://testflight.apple.com/join/K1rpGhxk).

It's still an alpha, so confusing bits and rough edges are exactly what I'm trying to find. Thanks for taking a look!
